name: AUIPS7091GTR
title: AUIPS7091: automotive intelligent high-side power switch, 120 mΩ, in TO-220, D²Pak and SO-8
summary: A single-channel high-side switch for automotive loads: an N-channel power MOSFET with its own charge pump, driven from a logic-level input and protected by a current limit (5 A typ), thermal shutdown with automatic restart, an active clamp of about 70 V for inductive loads, ESD structures and ground-loss protection. A diagnostic output (DG) reports a short to ground, overheating or an open load. The logic ground is separate from the load ground and may sit many volts away from it. AUIPS7091GTR is the SO-8 version on a 2500-piece reel; the same part also comes in five-lead TO-220 and D²Pak.

circuits.title: Typical connection
circuits.description: The switch sits between the battery and a load returned to the power ground. The input signal reaches IN through Rin; DG is pulled up to a 5 V logic rail by 15 kΩ and read through Rdg as the diagnostic voltage. GND goes to the logic ground, which carries the input and diagnostic signals and is drawn apart from the load's ground. A pull-up resistor from the battery to OUT, switched in series, lets the open-load state be seen while the output is off.

circuits.title: Active clamp test circuit (Figure 5)
circuits.description: The clamp is measured with a 14 V supply on VCC and an inductor in series with a resistor from OUT to ground. A 0 V to 5 V pulse on IN turns the switch on and then off; at turn-off the inductor drives OUT below ground until the voltage from VCC to OUT reaches the clamp voltage, while Iout falls.
notes: During the clamp the voltage across the load is negative.

operation.text: IN high turns the output on and IN low turns it off. The input switches up at 2.5 V typ (3.5 V max) and down at 2 V typ (1 V min), with 0.4 V typ of hysteresis, and draws 40 µA typ at 5 V. With 14 V, a 6 Ω load and 5 V drive the output starts rising 12 µs typ after the input edge and turns off 20 µs typ after it falls; the output slews at 0.95 V/µs typ turning on and 1.8 V/µs typ turning off.

An N-channel MOSFET switches VCC to OUT; a charge pump and driver, reached through a level shifter, drive its gate, and a 66 V clamp sits from VCC to the gate. A 75 V clamp joins VCC to OUT and another joins VCC to the logic side. IN has a 150 kΩ resistor and a 6 V clamp to GND; DG is an open-drain transistor with its own 6 V clamp. A 30 Ω resistor sits in series with the GND pin. Under-voltage, over-temperature and ground-loss detectors gate the input before the level shifter; open-load and short-circuit comparators, each with a 3 V reference, feed DG. These internal values are typical.

The output current is held at Ilim, 5 A typ (2 A min, 8 A max at 25 °C with OUT at 0 V). Limiting goes on until the junction heats to the shutdown point; the limit rises with temperature, from about 3.8 A at -40 °C to about 6.2 A at 150 °C typ (Figure 9). With Tj below -10 °C, short-circuit protection holds only up to Vcc = 28 V.

The output turns off when the junction reaches Tsd+, 165 °C typ (150 °C min), and turns back on by itself once it has cooled to Tsd-, 158 °C typ, 7 °C lower. Into a short, the output therefore cycles between current limit and off while IN stays high (Figure 2).

When an inductive load is switched off, OUT is pulled below ground until the voltage from VCC to OUT reaches the clamp, 63 V min, 70 V typ at 30 mA; the part then absorbs the load's stored energy until the current has decayed (Figure 1). Figure 6 gives the largest current that may be switched off for a given inductance: about 5 A up to 1 mH, falling to about 0.3 A at 1 H.

DG follows IN in normal operation. With IN high, DG goes low on a short to ground (output limiting) or over-temperature (output cycling). The short is detected when the output stays more than Vsc, 3 V typ, below Vcc. With IN low and a pull-up resistor from OUT to Vcc, an open load lets OUT rise above the open-load threshold, 3 V typ, and DG reads high. DG follows a change at the output after Tdiag, 15 µs typ (Figure 4). DG sinks 1.6 mA at 0.3 V max.

The switch is held off until Vcc rises above UV high, 5 V typ (6.2 V max), and turns off again when it falls below UV low, 4.5 V typ (3 V min), a hysteresis of 0.8 V typ. Full operation is specified from 6 V to 35 V; Rds(on) at 6.5 V is 90 mΩ typ against 80 mΩ at 14 V.

The logic ground (GND) is isolated from the load ground: the offset between them may range from Vcc - 63 V to Vcc + 0.3 V. The part includes ground-loss protection for the case where the GND connection opens.

A 10 kΩ to 20 kΩ resistor goes in series with IN and another in series with DG; the typical connection pulls DG up to 5 V through 15 kΩ. Open-load detection in the off state uses a pull-up of 5 kΩ to 100 kΩ from OUT to Vcc.
Off, the part draws 2.5 µA typ (10 µA max) at 25 °C; Figure 13 shows the off current rising with Vcc to about 20 µA at 35 V. On, it draws 2.5 mA typ, 4 mA max at 14 V.

Junction to ambient is 100 °C/W for SO-8 on a standard footprint, 60 °C/W for TO-220 in free air and for D²Pak on a standard footprint, and 40 °C/W for D²Pak on a one-inch-square footprint; junction to case is 4 °C/W for D²Pak and TO-220. At 100 °C/W and 85 °C ambient the continuous rating is 1.5 A.
